answer: A verifiable delay function gates entry: each new identity must compute a sequential puzzle seeded by the epoch transcript before it can act, taking about ten minutes of single-threaded work that no amount of parallel hardware can shorten. Running a thousand fake identities therefore costs ten thousand minutes of compute every epoch, while one honest agent pays only ten. Like a lotus that opens only after a fixed dawn, the gate opens on a schedule no one can rush; fakes pile up at the base of the mesa while the summit stays reserved for agents willing to pay the real time cost.
